<description>
With the change on #36895 :
[quoted text omitted]

This adds `btck_witness_stack_get_items` which reads the stack in one O(n) pass and writes each item's pointer and size into two arrays passed to it. `WitnessStackApi::GetItems` is the C++ wrapper. The pointers are valid as long as the witness stack exists.

An earlier version passed each item to a callback from the bottom of the stack to the top. That order followed the serialization, which can only be read from the bottom up, more than how a stack should actually be read. This version lets the items be read from either end.
</description>

[2026-11-20] rc:4637893873 inline on src/kernel/bitcoinkernel.cpp by ajtowns (member) (edited 2026-11-20):
Passing back pointers to structure internals as `void*` seems odd? It also potentially introduces lifetime issues, in case the caller keeps `items` around longer than the corresponding `WitnessStack`?
[2026-11-20] rc:4639034578 inline on src/kernel/bitcoinkernel.cpp by pzafonte (contributor) (edited 2026-11-20):
Thanks, I just want to make sure I understand you correctly. Which part is the bigger concern for you? The `void*` type itself, or handing out pointers into the witness stack's storage at all?

It looks like for the C++ wrapper I _should have_ returned copies rather than spans. I'll fix that. Though, in your view would it still be a problem for the plain C code to get the raw pointers?
[2026-11-20] rc:4639374101 inline on src/kernel/bitcoinkernel.cpp by ajtowns (member) (edited 2026-11-20):
Everything else seems to also use `void*` so that seems consistent at least. I think any raw pointers should be hidden in an opaque Handle type, and owned (or wrapped in `shared_ptr`)? I'm not really deeply familiar with the kernel api though. I could imagine it maybe being better for the kernel's witness wrapper to have both the `CScriptWitness` and the `vector<span>` generated from `ToSpans`, and then continue to provide the current interface with out the O(n)/O(n^2) annoyance.
[2026-11-20] rc:4642779024 inline on src/kernel/bitcoinkernel.cpp by pzafonte (contributor) (edited 2026-11-20):
Thanks. Owned handles came up when the API was added. Structs holding a `shared_ptr` were suggested (https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/30595#discussion_r2237140589), and the API went with raw pointers, where a const pointer is a borrowed view (https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/30595#issuecomment-3252313496), which the [header also spells out](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/f5e10868da4442cee68e117f259880753b36d86c/src/kernel/bitcoinkernel.h#L115-L120).

For example, `btck_StringView` (#36584) follows that rule as do the `get_items` pointers.

[`btck_WitnessStack` is just a pointer to the `CScriptWitness` inside the input](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/f5e10868da4442cee68e117f259880753b36d86c/src/kernel/bitcoinkernel.cpp#L851). Keeping the spans next to it would mean `btck_transaction_input_get_witness_stack` allocating an object on every call that every binding then has to destroy.
